verses.138:1: Senhor, vós me provastes, e me conhecestes: * vós conhecestes {sessio}.
verses.138:3: De longe entendestes os meus pensamentos: * {investigasti} a minha vereda e {funiculus}.
verses.138:4: E previstes todos os meus caminhos: * porque não há palavra na minha língua.
verses.138:5: Eis, Senhor, que vós conhecestes todas as coisas, as últimas e as antigas: * vós me formastes, e pusestes sobre mim a vossa mão.
verses.138:6: Maravilhoso se tornou o vosso saber {exme}: * fortaleceu-se, e não {potero}.
verses.138:7: {quo} irei, {aspiritu} do vosso espírito? * e {quo2} fugirei da vossa face?
verses.138:8: Se eu subir ao céu, vós estais ali: * se eu descer ao {infernum}, estais presente.
verses.138:9: Se eu tomar {pennas} ao amanhecer, * e habitar nos extremos do mar:
verses.138:10: Pois também ali a vossa mão me guiará: * e me {tenebit} a vossa direita.
verses.138:11: E eu disse: Talvez as trevas {conculcabunt}: * e a noite {nox} a minha luz nas minhas delícias.
verses.138:12: Porque as trevas {obscurabuntur} para vós, † e a noite se iluminará como o dia: * como as suas trevas, assim também a sua luz.
verses.138:13: Porque vós possuístes os meus rins: * vós me amparastes desde {utero} da minha mãe.
verses.138:14: Eu vos darei graças, porque fostes engrandecido {terribiliter}: ‡ maravilhosas são as vossas obras, * e a minha alma {cognoscit} {nimis14}.
verses.138:15: Não vos foram ocultos {os}, que fizestes em oculto: * e o meu ser nas partes mais baixas da terra.
verses.138:16: Os vossos olhos me viram {imperfectum}, † e no vosso livro todos serão escritos: * dias serão formados, e ninguém neles.
verses.138:17: {mihi}, {nimis17} foram honrados os vossos amigos, Deus: * {nimis17b} se fortaleceu {principatus}.
verses.138:18: Eu os contarei, e se multiplicarão {superarenam}: * {exsurrexi}, e ainda estou convosco.
verses.138:19: {si} matardes, Deus, os pecadores: * homens de sangue, apartai-vos de mim:
verses.138:20: Porque dizeis em pensamento: * {accipient} as vossas cidades.
verses.138:21: Não odiava eu, Senhor, os que vos odeiam? * e não definhava por causa dos vossos inimigos?
verses.138:22: Com ódio perfeito eu os odiava: * e eles se tornaram meus inimigos.
verses.138:23: Provai-me, Deus, e {scito} o meu coração: * interrogai-me, e conhecei as minhas veredas.
verses.138:24: E vede se há em mim caminho de iniquidade: * e guiai-me no caminho eterno.

decisions.latin: tu cognovísti sessiónem meam, et resurrectiónem meam
decisions.why: Two nouns (καθέδραν … ἔγερσιν): my sitting and my rising. *resurréctio* in Church Latin is the word for resurrection (Lewis & Short know no other sense), and this very colon is the verse of the Easter Sunday Introit (missa Pasc0-0) — the Church hears the risen Christ in it, and the Fathers read *sessio* / *resurrectio* as passion and resurrection. The plain sense is sitting down and getting up. Ruled: two nominal infinitives, *o meu sentar e o meu ressurgir* — nouns as the Latin, the plain image of sitting and rising, and *ressurgir* (the glossary's verb for *resúrgere*, Ps 1:5, 40:9) keeps the rising-again that the Easter use hears, without forcing it. Cost: *o meu ressurgir* after a sitting is less plain than *levantar*.

options.label: o meu sentar e o meu ressurgir

forms.sessio: o meu sentar e o meu ressurgir

options.note: Draft. Nouns kept as nominal infinitives; the resúrgere row's verb keeps the Easter echo open.

options.label: o meu assento e a minha ressurreição

forms.sessio: o meu assento e a minha ressurreição

options.note: The Latin's nouns word for word; the Easter sense spoken outright, the plain sense (getting up) lost — *assento* is a seat.

options.label: o meu sentar e o meu levantar

forms.sessio: o meu sentar e o meu levantar

options.note: The plain image only; the Easter echo gone.

options.label: quando me sento e quando me levanto

forms.sessio: quando me sento e quando me levanto

options.note: MS1932 (*tu sabes quando me sento e quando me levanto*); the CNBB's line from the Hebrew is close (circulation.md). Nouns turned to clauses; the Easter echo gone.

decisions.latin: sémitam meam, et funículum meum investigásti
decisions.why: *funículus* (σχοῖνος) is a cord, a measuring line; beside *sémita* it is the line a life is laid out by (DRB 'my line'; MS1932 *o fio da minha carreira* explains). The glossary's *funículus → corda* (77:54b, 104:11) keeps the image. *investigáre* is to track by footprints (*vestigium*; ἐξιχνιάζω, 'follow the track'); *investigar* is its cognate and plain. Kept.

options.label: investigastes … a minha corda
options.note: Draft. The glossary's *corda*; the cognate verb. The Latin's order (object first) turned to Portuguese order.

options.label: rastreastes … a minha corda
options.note: The track-following of *in-vestig-áre* made concrete; *rastrear* is also heard as surveillance.

options.label: investigastes … o meu fio
options.note: MS1932's word (*o fio da minha carreira*), without his gloss; leaves the glossary's *corda*.

decisions.latin: Mirábilis facta est sciéntia tua ex me
decisions.why: *ex me* (ἐξ ἐμοῦ) renders the Hebrew comparative *mimmenni* ('too wonderful for me'), but a Latin reader can also hear 'from me' or 'of me' — God's knowledge made wonderful from what he did in me (Augustine's reading). v1 ruled for MS1932's *acima de mim*, the comparison 6b supports; the v1 Latinist (minor) showed it closes what the Latin leaves open. v2 takes the preposition's own word, *de mim*: 'of me / from me' stays audible and 6b still says the knowledge is out of reach (D2). The colon is also in the Easter Introit; *o vosso saber* is the sciéntia row's word.

options.label: de mim
options.note: v2, the v1 Latinist's fix: the preposition, the Latin's openness kept.

options.label: acima de mim
options.note: v1; MS1932 *Maravilhosa acima de mim*. The comparison, as 6b supports; resolves the ambiguity.

options.label: para mim
options.note: DRB 'is become wonderful to me'.

options.label: a partir de mim
options.note: The preposition's source sense (Augustine); explains more than it says.

decisions.latin: confortáta est, et non pótero ad eam
decisions.why: *non pótero ad eam* has no infinitive ('I shall not be able [to reach] to it'); Portuguese needs one. *confortáta est* keeps the glossary's *fortalecer-se* (ἐκραταιώθη) — the Latin says 'grew strong', not the Hebrew's 'is high'.

options.label: poderei alcançá-lo
options.note: Draft. The verb supplied; MS1932 *não poderei atingi-la*.

options.label: poderei chegar até ele
options.note: *ad eam* kept as *até*; longer.

decisions.why: *ire a* is 'go away from'; *ir do vosso espírito* is not Portuguese. *longe* supplies the separation *a* carries; the second colon *fugirei da vossa face* (as 67:2 *fujam da sua face*; the CNBB's line has the same words, circulation.md) needs nothing. *Quo … quo* → *Aonde … aonde* (the verb of motion takes *aonde*); the parallel of the two questions kept, and the first colon one syllable shorter than *Para onde* (checks flagged +6).

options.label: longe
options.note: Draft. DM1962 has the same build (*Aonde irei longe do teu espírito*).

options.label: fugindo
options.note: Anticipates 7b's verb.

options.label: Para onde … para onde
options.note: MS1932's *Para onde*; +2 syllables in a colon already long against the Latin's nine.

decisions.why: The inférnus row names 138:8 as one of its hard tests: God present in the *inferno*. The Latin's word is kept, as in every translated place (6:6, 15:10, 29:4 …). Here the hell of the damned is not a wrong sense: God's presence even there is the point of the verse. The CNBB (from the Hebrew) has *abismo*; the Vatican's Portuguese Easter message of 2008 quotes *se descer aos infernos* (circulation.md).

options.label: inferno
options.note: Draft; the row.

options.label: mundo dos mortos
options.note: The row's option (Ps 29).

decisions.why: The Latin (and the Greek τὰς πτέρυγάς μου κατ' ὄρθρον) says *my* wings, at daybreak — not the Hebrew's 'wings of the dawn' that the CNBB prays (*Se a aurora me emprestar as suas asas*). *penna* is feather and wing; *asas* is the plain word. *dilúculo* → *ao amanhecer* as 56:9 = 107:3.

options.label: as minhas asas
options.note: Draft. The Latin's possessive kept.

options.label: as minhas penas
options.note: The cognate; *penas* is heard first as 'sorrows'.

decisions.why: The tenére row (open) has *tomar* in Ps 72 for a pair that must match there (pride seizing, God holding). Here there is no pair; the sense is holding fast. *segurar* is the row's own named option, plain, and the CNBB's verb here. Proposed for the row: *segurar* where *tenére* is God holding a person and no pair binds. v2: the second colon follows the Latin order (*et tenébit me déxtera tua → e me segurará a vossa direita*), which also breaks the v1 *guiará / segurará* rhyme at mediant and final (the v1 stylist).

options.label: segurará
options.note: Draft.

options.label: tomará
options.note: MS1932 *me tomará a tua direita*; the tenére row's word from Ps 72.

decisions.why: *fórsitan → talvez* (row). Portuguese puts *talvez* before a verb with the subjunctive; the Latin has a future. *conculcáre → calcar aos pés* (D44; this verse is on the row's list). Ps 7's readers stumbled on the subjunctive *calque*; the plural *calquem* is the form here. The future (*me calcarão aos pés*) keeps the Latin's tense but is school-grammar wrong after a leading *talvez*.

options.label: me calquem aos pés
options.note: Draft. The row's verb in the mood Portuguese needs.

options.label: me calcarão aos pés
options.note: The Latin's future; colloquial after *talvez*.

options.label: me pisem
options.note: The v1 stylist: plainer, but leaves the conculcáre row and loses the *con-*.

decisions.latin: et nox illuminátio mea in delíciis meis
decisions.why: Verbless in the Latin and the Greek. A copula must be supplied for a Portuguese sentence; the future follows *conculcábunt* inside the same supposed speech (DRB 'and night shall be my light'). *illuminátio → luz* (row, 26:1); *delíciæ* (τρυφή) → *delícias*, the word 35:9 gives *voluptas* for the same Greek τρυφή (D15's test).

options.label: será
options.note: Draft; DRB.

options.label: é
options.note: Present: a statement, not part of the fear.

decisions.latin: Quia ténebræ non obscurabúntur a te
decisions.why: Future passive with *a te* (ἀπὸ σοῦ): the darkness will not be dark to God. *por vós* would make God the one who darkens (a wrong sense); *para vós* is DRB's 'to thee'. The medio-passive keeps the verb.

options.label: não se escurecerão
options.note: Draft.

options.label: não serão escuras
options.note: MS1932 *não são escuras* (present); the verb turned to an adjective.

decisions.latin: suscepísti me de útero matris meæ
decisions.why: The *úterus* row: *seio* with *materno* (21:10, 70:6) because bare *seio* is the breast; here *da minha mãe* does the same work — *o seio da minha mãe* is heard as the womb (the CNBB has *no seio de minha mãe* in this psalm, circulation.md). *ventre* stays *venter*'s. *suscípere* (a person) → *amparar* (D19).

options.label: o seio
options.note: Draft; the row.

options.label: o ventre
options.note: Plainest, but it is venter's word (21:11, 70:6b *desde o ventre da minha mãe*).

decisions.why: The Latin has God magnified (2nd person), where the Greek has ἐθαυμαστώθην (1st person, 'I was made wonderful') and the Hebrew likewise: the Latin is translated. *terríbilis → terrível* is settled (D43); the adverb *terrivelmente* is heard in Brazil as 'extremely' or 'badly', so the phrase *de modo terrível* keeps the root without the slang. *magnificáre → engrandecer* (row).

options.label: de modo terrível
options.note: Draft.

options.label: terrivelmente
options.note: The adverb; everyday 'awfully'. The v1 stylist asked for it in the Latin order (*porque terrivelmente fostes engrandecido*).

options.label: de modo tremendo
options.note: Awe without the everyday 'horrible'; leaves the terríbilis row.

decisions.latin: cognóscit nimis … nimis honorificáti sunt … nimis confortátus est
decisions.why: Three times in the psalm, twice in one verse (17), where the repetition is the Latin's figure and must stay. The nimis row has no single rendering; *sem medida* (118:138, 45:2, 78:8, 106:38, 108:30, 115:1) keeps the 'beyond measure' that *nimis* says, where *muito* (47:2, as valde) flattens it. One word for all three places. 138:17 is the Apostles' Introit, Gradual and responsory (missa Sancti 02-24, 11-29; Commune C1) — the line will be said alone.

options.label: sem medida
options.note: Draft. The row's most-used rendering.

options.label: muito
options.note: As 47:2 (valde's word); plainer, weaker. In 14 it needs *bem*.

options.label: sobremaneira
options.note: MS1932 in 17 (*honraste sobremaneira*); unknown to earlier blind readers (118:96, 30:12).

decisions.why: *cognóscit* has no object; *conhecer* wants one (the cognóscere row: collocation governs). The object is plainly the works just named; *o* (neuter: 'it, this') is the lightest supply and does not narrow it to the works. The psalter's antiphon *Mirabília ópera tua, Dómine, et ánima mea cognóscit nimis* is said with this colon.

options.label: o conhece
options.note: Draft; MS1932 *o conhece de sobra*.

options.label: as conhece
options.note: The works named as object.

options.label: o sabe
options.note: The row's *saber* where there is no noun object (13:4).

decisions.latin: Non est occultátum os meum a te, quod fecísti in occúlto
decisions.why: *os meum* (τὸ ὀστοῦν μου) is a collective singular, the frame of the body. *o meu osso* is heard as one bone; the plural is how Portuguese says it (MS1932 *Os meus ossos*); number is grammar (D2). The Latin's echo *occultátum … in occúlto* is kept (*ocultos … em oculto*). 15b keeps *et*, not *nem*: *substántia mea* can hang on *non est occultátum* or on *fecísti*, and the Latin leaves it open. *substántia → o meu ser* (D39, which names 138:15); *inferióra terræ → as partes mais baixas da terra* (62:10; the row names 138:15).

options.label: os meus ossos
options.note: Draft; MS1932.

options.label: o meu osso
options.note: The Latin's number (DRB 'my bone'); heard as a single bone.

decisions.why: A neuter adjective as noun, 'my unfinished (being)' (ἀκατέργαστον, 'unwrought'). L&S: *imperféctus* is first 'unfinished, incomplete'. The cognate *imperfeito* is heard today first as 'flawed' — the moral sense, which the Latin can carry (Augustine applies it to the weaker members of the Church) but not first. Ruled: *inacabado*, the plainer word for the first sense, with the noun turned to a predicate on *me* (grammar). *ser* is not supplied because 138:15 already spends it on *substántia*.

options.label: inacabado
options.note: Draft.

options.label: imperfeito
options.note: The cognate; heard as 'flawed' first — both senses the Latin can have.

options.label: ainda informe
options.note: MS1932 *quando era ainda informe*.

decisions.why: The dative of the one who judges: 'to me, in my eyes'. *Mas para mim* keeps the dative and the *autem*. MS1932's *Mas eu vejo que* explains it. The Apostles' Introit (02-24) keeps *Mihi autem*; the Gradual and the responsories drop it — the colon reads without it.

options.label: Mas para mim
options.note: Draft.

options.label: Para mim, porém
options.note: *autem* after, as the Latin places it; heavier.

options.label: Mas para mim, Deus, … os vossos amigos
options.note: The v1 stylist moved the vocative forward (*ó Deus*). Not taken: the bare *Deus* is house style, and the Apostles' Gradual lifts *Nimis honoráti sunt amíci tui, Deus* without *Mihi autem*, so the vocative has to stay in the colon's end.

decisions.why: *principátus* (αἱ ἀρχαί) is rule, pre-eminence (L&S). The cognate *principado* is heard in Brazil as a prince's territory (Monaco) — or as the angelic order. *domínio* is already shared by three Latin words (dominátio, impérium, potéstas: rows 85:16, 113:2). D44 gave the adjective *principális* → *soberano* (50:14); *soberania* keeps that family. The CNBB's line (from the Hebrew) is about God's thoughts, not his friends: no help.

options.label: a sua soberania
options.note: Draft. The principális family (D44).

options.label: o seu principado
options.note: The cognate (DRB 'principality').

options.label: o seu império
options.note: MS1932; *império* was refused at 85:16 as 'empire'.

options.label: o seu domínio
options.note: Plain; a fourth Latin word on *domínio*.

decisions.why: *super* is the comparison (ὑπὲρ ἄμμον), as 17:18 *super me* → *mais do que eu*. *sobre a areia* would be heard as 'on the sand'.

options.label: mais que a areia
options.note: Draft.

options.label: além da areia
options.note: Keeps *super* as a preposition.

decisions.why: *exsúrgere → levantar-se* (row; 3:6 *e me levantei*, the same *exsurréxi*). The Easter Introit reads *Resurréxi* (the Roman psalter's word) where this psalter has *exsurréxi*; this text follows the psalter, and a Missal translation would render *Resurréxi* by its own verb. Circulating Portuguese renderings of the Introit (*Ressuscitei, estou convosco para sempre*; *ressuscitei e estou sempre contigo*; circulation.md) belong to that word, not this one. *adhuc → ainda* (not *para sempre*).

options.label: levantei-me
options.note: Draft; the row.

options.label: despertei
options.note: ἐξηγέρθην as waking (MS1932 *Quando desperto*); leaves the row.

options.label: ressurgi
options.note: The Easter Introit's *Resurréxi*; the resúrgere row's verb, not exsúrgere's.

decisions.why: A protasis with no apodosis (ἐὰν ἀποκτείνῃς): the Hebrew *'im* here is a wish ('O that you would slay'), and MS1932 turns it into a question (*Não acabarás … ?*). The Latin says *Si*; the ellipsis is kept, as the Latin keeps it. *occídere → matar* (row).

options.label: Se
options.note: Draft; DRB 'If thou wilt kill'.

options.label: Oxalá
options.note: The wish reading (the Hebrew's sense); it resolves what the Latin leaves open.

decisions.why: *accípere → receber* (row); *in vanitáte* (εἰς ματαιότητα) → *em vão*, the phrase's Portuguese form (*receber na vaidade* is not said); the vánitas row's *vaidade* is for the noun standing alone. **A cost of *vós*:** *civitátes tuas* is God's (singular), inside a speech of men addressed as *vós* (*dícitis*, plural); in Portuguese *as vossas cidades* can be heard as the men's. v1 wrote *vós dizeis* (the Ps 10:2 remedy) to name the speakers; both v1 readers (stylist, ambiguity) heard that stressed *vós* as God, the psalm's addressee everywhere else. v2 drops it, as the Latin has no pronoun (*dícitis*): the plural ending after *apartai-vos* marks the men; *as vossas cidades* stays open. MS1932 glosses a whole subject in (*os justos possuirão*); not followed.

options.label: Receberão em vão
options.note: Draft.

options.label: Tomarão em vão
options.note: The accípere row's option (DRB 23:4 'taken in vain'); heard as the commandment's 'take in vain'.

decisions.latin: Proba me, Deus, et scito cor meum: intérroga me, et cognósce sémitas meas
decisions.why: The Latin varies *scito … cognósce*; the Greek has γνῶθι twice. By D15's Greek test one verb serves, and the scire row already gives *conhecer* (118:125). *conhecei* is safe at the vós imperative (past *conheci*). *Provai-me* as 25:2; *interrogai-me* as the interrogáre row foresaw.

options.label: conhecei
options.note: Draft; the scire row; the Greek's repetition heard.

options.label: sabei
options.note: Keeps the Latin's two verbs apart; *sabei o meu coração* is not said.

options.label: sondai
options.note: MS1932 *sonda o meu coração*; scrutári's word (7:10), refused.

choices.138:1: No titulus (*In finem, Psalmus David* in the LXX and MS1932; not in DO's Latin): D7. *vós* supplied in 1a for a sayable opening with proclisis; 1b's *vós* is the Latin's *tu*. The verse number (2) inside the Latin is not reproduced. The whole verse is the Easter Introit's psalm verse and the Introit verse of 02-24 (circulation.md). *probáre → provar* (the examináre / probáre row, as 16:3, 25:2). The CNBB's familiar *vós me sondais e conheceis* is from the Hebrew: *sondar* is scrutári's word here.
choices.138:3: *intellígere → entender*; *de longe* moved to the head (natural order). *sémita → vereda* (D15).
choices.138:4: *sermo → palavra* (D15). The Latin (with the Greek) says only that there is no word on my tongue; MS1932 and the CNBB add 'before it / you know it all' (the Hebrew) — not added.
choices.138:5: *Ecce → Eis que* (the ecce row, 127:4). *novíssima … antíqua* → *as últimas e as antigas* with *coisas* supplied once; the *novíssima* row (72:17, *o fim deles*) is another build. 5b is in the Easter Introit.
choices.138:8: *illic → ali* (row). *ades → estais presente* (the CNBB has the same words, from the Hebrew).
choices.138:9: *extréma maris* → *os extremos do mar*; plural kept.
choices.138:10: *Étenim* (καὶ γάρ) → *Pois também*; *illuc* (whither) → *ali*, the row's word. *dedúcere → guiar* (D22; this verse is on the row's list).
choices.138:12: The middle colon *et nox sicut dies illuminábitur* → *e a noite se iluminará como o dia*: the medio-passive (MS1932 *a noite é clara como o dia*) and Portuguese order; the Latin-order *e a noite, como o dia, será iluminada* was +4 syllables. *sicut ténebræ ejus, ita et lumen ejus* → *como as suas trevas, assim também a sua luz* — *ejus* (the night's) kept as open as the Latin; *lumen → luz* (row). *illumináre → iluminar*.
choices.138:13: *possidére → possuir* (row); *renes → rins* (row; MS1932's gloss *afectos* not followed).
choices.138:14: *Confitébor tibi → Eu vos darei graças* (D5). *mirabília ópera tua* verbless in the Latin; copula supplied. The ‡ is kept.
choices.138:16: *omnes scribéntur* keeps the future and leaves *todos* open (all men, all days, all members); MS1932 glosses *os mortais*. *dies formabúntur, et nemo in eis* kept verbless in its second half, as the Latin: the Latin's riddle (the Hebrew's 'when as yet there was none of them') is not resolved.
choices.138:17: The Latin's own departure from the Hebrew: *amíci tui* (God's friends, honoured) where the Hebrew has 'thy thoughts, how precious'. Translated as the Latin. *honorificáre → honrar* (D44; this is the row's 'other place'). The Missal and the Office read *honoráti* (the same sense). The two *sem medida* stand at the head of each colon's predicate so the repetition is heard.
choices.138:19: *viri sánguinum → homens de sangue* (D29, row); *declináte a me → apartai-vos de mim* (118:115).
choices.138:21: *óderam* (pluperfect of a perfect-with-present-sense verb) → the imperfect *odiava*; *odérunt te* → *vos odeiam* (the odísse row, 24:19). *tabéscere → definhar* (row; 138:21 is the near twin of 118:158 *e definhava*). *super* → *por causa de* (DRB 'because of').
choices.138:22: *Perfécto ódio óderam illos* → *Com ódio perfeito eu os odiava* (the odísse row names this build). checks flags 138:21/22 ending both on *inimigos*: the Latin ends both on *inimícos / inimíci* — the echo is the Latin's, kept.
choices.138:24: *deduc me in via ætérna* → *guiai-me no caminho eterno* (D22). *via iniquitátis* without article in the Latin → *caminho de iniquidade*, without article as the Latin (MS1932 has the same words).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from the parallels (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, DM1962, MS1932), glossary rows looked up term by term (`gloss_lookup.py`), liturgical uses by grep and Brazilian circulation fetched (`circulation.md`). Hard readings: 138:1 *resurrectiónem* (the Easter Introit's verse), 138:6 *ex me*, 138:16 *imperféctum* and *dies formabúntur, et nemo in eis*, 138:17 *amíci tui* and *principátus* (the Apostles' texts), 138:20 *civitátes tuas* inside a plural address.

Hard checks pass. Soft: 138:7a was +6 → *Aonde* (−2; still +5, the Latin colon is nine syllables and *longe* is needed for *a*); 138:12 middle colon +4 → reordered (*se iluminará como o dia*); 138:24a +3 → article dropped. Accepted: 138:1b −5 (the nominal infinitives are short), 138:3a −3, 138:6a +3 (the Easter Introit line, every word needed), 138:8b +3 (*estais presente* for *ades*), 138:9a +3 (*ao amanhecer* for *dilúculo*), 138:14b and 138:17b +3 (*sem medida*), 138:15b −3, 138:20b −3, 138:21b +3 (*não* repeated for the second question). The 21/22 *inimigos* rhyme is the Latin's own echo.

outcomes: 138:6 *ex me → acima de mim* resolves the Latin's ambiguity: taken, *de mim* (decision exme).
138:15 *os meum* made plural: declined. Collective singular; *o meu osso* is heard as one bone, number is grammar (D2); kept as option.
138:15 *substántia → o meu ser* too abstract: declined. D39 settles *o meu ser* and names 138:15.
138:5 drop the first *vós*: declined. The Latin's *tu … tu* is a repetition D2 keeps.
138:10 *guiará / segurará* rhyme: taken, *e me segurará a vossa direita* (the Latin order).
138:11 *me calquem aos pés → me pisem*: declined, conculcáre row (D44); kept as option.
138:14 *de modo terrível → terrivelmente*: declined. The adverb is heard as 'awfully'; the option notes the request.
138:17 vocative forward (*ó Deus*): declined. Bare *Deus* is house style, and the Apostles' Gradual lifts the colon without *Mihi autem*, so *Deus* stays at its end; kept as option.
138:20 drop *vós*: taken, *Porque dizeis em pensamento* (the Latin has no pronoun), so the ear no longer hears God speaking.

audit.note: Thirty-three items, mostly the Latin's own.
outcomes: 138:20 *vós* heard as God: fixed by the stylist's change (*Porque dizeis*). *as vossas cidades* stays God's cities (*civitátes tuas*) inside a plural address; the Latin is as obscure.
138:1 *o meu ressurgir* heard as resurrection: intended; the verse is the Easter Introit.

Kept as the Latin's own obscurities: 138:3 *corda*, 138:4, 138:11b, 138:12 *suas*, 138:16 *todos* and *ninguém neles*, 138:17 *sua soberania*, 138:18 *Eu os contarei*, 138:19 the open conditional, 138:20b.
Unknown words (*vereda, calquem, amparastes, matardes, definhava*) are all settled glossary rows; not changed.
